workflows.name: Triage a Python error with Stack Overflow and the official Python docs
steps: In the Stack Overflow tab, click the search box, type "{error}" and press Enter
Open the top question; note its title and the vote count of the accepted (or highest-voted) answer
Switch to the Python docs tab, type "{module}" in the Quick search box and press Enter; open the {module} page from the results
Note the first sentence of the page, then click the Python logo to return to the docs home
Switch to Notes, click "New note", type "{error}: see SO '<title>' (<votes> votes). Docs {module}: <first sentence>" and press Enter

workflows.name: Pull a country's GDP and population from the World Bank and email a client brief
steps: In the World Bank Data tab, click the search box, type {country} and press Enter; open the {country} country page
Note the latest GDP (current US$) and population figures with their year
Scroll down to GDP growth (annual %) and note the latest value
Switch to the Wikipedia tab, search "{country}" and open the article; note the capital and the currency from the infobox
Switch to the Mail tab, click To and type {client}@example.com, click Subject and type "{country} macro snapshot"
Click Body and type "Hi {client}, {country}: GDP <gdp> (<year>), growth <growth>%, population <population>; capital <capital>, currency <currency>." Do not click Send. Click Discard

workflows.name: Add a public-domain classic to a reading list from Project Gutenberg and the author's Wikipedia page
steps: In the Project Gutenberg tab, click the search box, type "{title}" and press Enter
Open the matching book by {author}; on its page note the release date and the downloads count. Do not download it
Switch to the Wikipedia tab, search "{author}" and open the article; note the birth and death years
Switch to Notes, click "New note", type "Read: {title} by {author} (<birth>-<death>), Gutenberg since <release date>, <downloads> downloads" and press Enter

noise.description: Open a new tab, go to news.ycombinator.com, scroll the front page, open one comment thread, close the tab
Open a new tab, go to bbc.com/news, scroll through the headlines, open one story, skim it, close the tab
Abandoned attempt: in the Project Gutenberg tab, search "Ulysses", scroll the results, then give up without opening any
Wander: click through the Notes, Mail and Stack Overflow tabs without doing anything, scroll the Notes list
Open a new tab, go to en.wikipedia.org, click Random article in the menu, skim it, close the tab
